blockers.quote: Mr. Halloran repairs the account map, and Theo runs it again.
blockers.why: Check #16 fails: the climax depends on an unplanted global loan-account map and authority to repay strangers' debts. The earlier clearing-file format only explains file syntax.
blockers.fix: At line 38 replace the clearing-file plant with: “Mr. Halloran emails Theo the loan-payoff batch template, including the creditor account map it requires. Theo saves it.”

blockers.why: Check #3 fails: the title’s doubling promise appears at the end of a twenty-second beat, not by about 0:15.
blockers.fix: Move it to the opening narration: “Every midnight, your money doubles. A month ago you checked this screen before ordering coffee. This morning you could buy the kiosk, the pier and the ship coming in.”

suggestions.fix: Clarify that this is Theo’s forecast, not a jump forward in chronology: “His program jumps ahead to day thirty-one: $1,073,741,824.”

suggestions.quote: One hyperinflation, one line: Hungary, 1946, prices doubling every fifteen hours (to source at G2).
suggestions.fix: Cut this detour and go directly from the atoms limit to Mr. Halloran’s day-forty-nine call, keeping the deadline moving.

suggestions.quote: The choice is morally live: three billion strangers' debts erased without anyone asking, and Mrs. Vance said no, and you keep that.
suggestions.fix: Make the dilemma playable rather than asserted: “You can save everyone’s money only by choosing for three billion people. No vote. No permission. If you refuse, their money breaks by morning.”

keep.quote: Not when it's new. Your double is her half.
The number grows; nothing it can buy does.
